job.style: a rule explained with two contrasting examples

passage: In mathematics, a fraction represents a part of a single whole, and for it to be valid, the whole must be divided into equal parts. For example, if you cut a circular pizza into two unequal pieces, you cannot call one piece 1/2 because the parts are not identical. A fraction is written as a numerator over a denominator, where the denominator shows the total number of equal parts in one whole. When comparing fractions like 1/4 and 1/5, remember that the denominator tells us how many pieces the whole is split into; therefore, 1/4 is larger than 1/5 because the whole is divided into fewer, larger sections. Furthermore, a mixed number like 2 1/3 is actually a sum, representing 2 wholes plus 1/3, not a multiplication of 2 and 1/3. Finally, when adding fractions, you must find a common denominator rather than simply adding the numerators and denominators together. For instance, to add 1/4 and 1/4, you keep the denominator the same and add the numerators to get 2/4, which simplifies to 1/2. Adding denominators would incorrectly result in 2/8, which is a smaller value than the actual sum.

items.evidence: For example, if you cut a circular pizza into two unequal pieces, you cannot call one piece 1/2 because the parts are not identical.
items.q: Meena cuts a roti into one big piece and one small piece. What are the pieces?
options: Neither piece is 1/2; their sizes differ
Each piece is 1/2; there are two pieces
The big piece is 1/2; it is larger
The small piece is 1/4; it is smaller
items.explain: A fraction needs equal parts, so unequal pieces cannot be called 1/2.

wrong.why: thinks any split into two parts makes halves
thinks the bigger share must be the half
guesses a fraction from the look of a small piece

items.evidence: When comparing fractions like 1/4 and 1/5, remember that the denominator tells us how many pieces the whole is split into; therefore, 1/4 is larger than 1/5 because the whole is divided into fewer, larger sections.
items.q: Ravi gets 1/5 of a cake and Sita gets 1/4 of the same cake. Who gets more?
options: Sita, since her pieces are fewer and bigger
Both, since each gets just one piece
Ravi, since his fraction has larger numbers
items.explain: Cutting into 4 gives fewer, larger pieces than cutting into 5, so 1/4 is more.

wrong.why: thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
looks only at the numerator 1 and ignores piece size
thinks larger numbers always mean a bigger fraction

items.evidence: Furthermore, a mixed number like 2 1/3 is actually a sum, representing 2 wholes plus 1/3, not a multiplication of 2 and 1/3.
items.q: Asha has 2 1/3 rotis in her tiffin. How much roti does she have?
options: Two whole rotis and one third of a roti
Two times one third of a roti
Only two thirds of one roti
Three rotis, from adding the 2 and 1
items.explain: A mixed number is a sum: 2 1/3 means 2 wholes plus 1/3.

wrong.why: thinks a mixed number means multiplying
treats the numbers as separate whole numbers

items.evidence: Adding denominators would incorrectly result in 2/8, which is a smaller value than the actual sum.
items.q: Karan adds 1/4 and 1/4 by adding tops and bottoms, getting 2/8. What is wrong?
options: It is less than the true sum, 1/2
It is more than the true sum, 1/2
It is equal to the true sum, 1/2
It is less than the true sum, 1/4
items.explain: The real sum is 2/4, which is 1/2; 2/8 is a smaller value.

wrong.why: thinks 2/8 is bigger because its numbers are larger
thinks adding tops and bottoms gives the right sum
picks the number 1/4 from the question as the sum
